claims.text: Clonidine PO: start 0.1 mg BID (morning and bedtime);
claims.quote: 0.1 mg tablet twice daily (morning and bedtime).

claims.text: ↑ by 0.1 mg/day at weekly intervals as needed;
claims.quote: Further increments of 0.1 mg per day may be made at weekly intervals if necessary until the desired response is achieved.
The therapeutic doses most commonly employed have ranged from 0.2 mg to 0.6 mg per day given in divided doses.

claims.text: On a beta-blocker too: stop the beta-blocker several days before tapering clonidine.
claims.quote: If therapy is to be discontinued in patients receiving a beta-blocker and clonidine concurrently, the beta-blocker should be withdrawn several days before the gradual discontinuation of clonidine hydrochloride.
If a patient receiving clonidine hydrochloride is also taking tricyclic antidepressants, the hypotensive effect of clonidine may be reduced, necessitating an increase in the clonidine dose.

claims.text: Watch HR with digoxin, CCBs or beta-blockers (sinus bradycardia).
claims.quote: Monitor heart rate in patients receiving clonidine concomitantly with agents known to affect sinus node function or AV nodal conduction, e.g. digitalis, calcium channel blockers and beta-blockers.

claims.text: Potentiates alcohol, barbiturates and other sedatives.
claims.quote: Clonidine may potentiate the CNS-depressive effects of alcohol, barbiturates or other sedating drugs.

claims.text: Rebound BP rise after stopping: reverse with oral clonidine or IV phentolamine.
claims.quote: An excessive rise in blood pressure following discontinuation of clonidine hydrochloride therapy can be reversed by administration of oral clonidine hydrochloride or by intravenous phentolamine.

claims.text: Overdose: early hypertension, then hypotension, bradycardia, respiratory depression, hypothermia, drowsiness, miosis;
claims.quote: Hypertension may develop early and may be followed by hypotension, bradycardia, respiratory depression, hypothermia, drowsiness, decreased or absent reflexes, weakness, irritability and miosis.
There is no specific antidote for clonidine overdosage.
